newsitem.title: USA: GM New York plant to get low-cost power.
newsitem.headline: GM New York plant to get low-cost power.

text.p: New York Power Authority said trustees Tuesday approved a proposed allocation of low-cost electricity for the General Motors Corp Powertrain plant in Massena, St. Lawrence County, N.Y., that would help to create or protect 380 jobs.

On August 6, GM Powertrain said the Massena plant will produce the cylinder block and head castings for a new lightweight global engine for the new model Saturn car and additional GM models sold around the world.
GM Powertrain's engine plant in Tonawanda will produce the engines.

In June, Power Authority trustees allocated 800 kilowatts of hydropower for the Tonawanda facility, which already receives 13,800 kilowatts of expansion power that helps to protect 3,706 jobs. Total employment there is about 4,200.
The proposed 8,000-kilowatt, 15-year allocation for the Massena facility now goes to Gov. George E. Pataki for his consideration, the authority said.
It said GM plans to invest $77 million for machinery and equipment at Massena.
The electricity would be produced at the Power Authority's James A. FitzPatrick Nuclear Power Plant on Lake Ontario near Oswego, NYPA said.
In seperate statements, the authority said 2,000 kilowatts of hydropower have been allocated to Sanborn, N.Y., facilities sold by British Petroleum Co Plc's Carborundum Co.

It also said trustees approved low-cost power for Kozy Shack Inc allowing the Hicksville, Long Island, producer of puddings and snack foods to proceed with a $1.9 million expansion instead of moving out of state. The company would get 300 kilowatts for 10 years and an additional short-term allocation of 400 kilowatts through 1997.
